text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- The Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox church, Aleksey II, is to start a three-day visit to Vilnius.
- French diplomat Patrick Donabedian who was beaten and robbed on Sunday was moved out of intensive care on Thursday. Doctors say he may be back at work in three months.
- The board of the central bank rejected a proposal to allow banks to issue foreign currency loans on the domestic market.
- Klaipeda prosecutor's office detained a former vice-president of bankrupt Vakaru Bankas on charges of misappropriating funds.
- Beer companies produced around 20 percent more beer in the first half of the year than the first half of last year. The market was led by Utenos followed by Kalnapilis and Shvyturys.
RESPUBLIKA
- The energy price commission decided to increase tariffs for hot water and heating.
- The central bank has registered a 14 million litas share issue by Siauliu Bank.
- The finance ministry is to issue 60 million litas of one-year T-bills.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas tells the newspaper that Lithuania was disappointed by the EU Commission's recommendations but would do all it could to be in the first wave of EU expansion.
- The reserves of the central bank exceeded one billion dollars and stood at $1.82 billion.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- Volkswagen cars sold most in the first half of 1997.
- The government will stop issuing state guarantees for loans taken by companies from next year.
- Biggest pharmaceuticals firm Sanitas made a four million litas net profit in the first half.
- The government is to discuss the agreement with UBS, who was the winner of a tender to advise on the sale of Lithuanian Telecom.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 223 517
